interview.question: To start things off, could you tell me a bit about yourself and what drew you to apply for this data analyst role with us?
interview.assesses: Overall background, communication style, and motivation for the role

interview.question: Looking at your internship experience, you built weekly sales dashboards and cleaned data using Python. Could you walk me through your exact process for cleaning a messy dataset before you start building a dashboard?
interview.assesses: Technical data preparation skills, attention to detail, and practical Python experience

interview.question: Our job description emphasizes presenting insights to non-technical managers. Can you tell me about a time when you had to explain a technical concept or complex data finding to someone without a technical background?
interview.assesses: Communication skills, ability to simplify complex data, and stakeholder management

interview.question: You mentioned building an AI speaking-coach web app as your final-year project, which is really interesting. Since presentation skills and confidence are a big focus there, how do you personally manage your own speaking pace and eye contact when presenting data to a large group?
interview.assesses: Self-awareness regarding presentation delivery, confidence, and non-verbal communication

interview.question: Imagine a non-technical retail manager comes to you asking for a sales forecast, but the historical data they provided is incomplete and inconsistent. How would you handle this request and what would you tell them?
interview.assesses: Problem-solving, business acumen, and professional communication under constraints

interview.question: Tell me about a time you led a team under pressure, like your university hackathon experience. How did you delegate tasks and keep everyone aligned to hit your deadline?
interview.assesses: Leadership, teamwork, time management, and conflict resolution

interview.question: That covers all the questions I have prepared for you today. Do you have any questions for us about the role, the team, or Nusantara Retail Group?
interview.assesses: Candidate engagement, curiosity, and preparation for the role

deck.title: Five Strategies for Effective Time Management
deck.summary: This concise three-slide presentation outlines practical time management strategies tailored for first-year students.
deck.main_message: Mastering simple daily habits like task prioritization and focused sprints will transform your academic and professional success.

slides.title: Five Strategies for Effective Time Management
slides.key_point: Introduce the five time management strategies and why they matter for new students.

slides.title: Plan and Prioritize
slides.key_point: Explain how to plan and prioritize using the Eisenhower matrix and daily task lists.

slides.title: Protect Your Focus
slides.key_point: Demonstrate how to protect focus through time-blocking and short work sprints.

qa: Could you explain a bit more about how we should use the Eisenhower matrix on slide 2 when most of our daily tasks feel urgent?
You mentioned five strategies in just three minutes on slide 1, but what is the single best habit for a beginner to start with tomorrow?
How do we handle it when our schedule changes completely day-to-day, making the rigid time-blocking on slide 3 hard to maintain?
Do you have any specific evidence or examples from your own experience showing that short work sprints actually improve study quality?
Are there specific free apps or tools you suggest for managing daily task lists and time blocking, or is paper better?
